page: OVHcloud c3-16-flex is a compute-optimized virtual instance powered by AMD EPYC x86_64 processors running on the KVM hypervisor. The configuration provides 8 dedicated physical cores mapped to 8 vCPUs running at a base clock of 2.3 GHz, with hyperthreading disabled (1.0 thread per core). The instance is allocated 16.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a 1:2 compute-to-memory profile (2.0 GB per core). Local storage consists of a 50 GB NVMe SSD, and networking is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps. No dedicated GPUs are included.

Benchmark data reflects solid execution capabilities across various compute tasks. Stress-ng single-core performance ranks in the top 25% with a score of 3,075.67, while multi-core performance aligns with the middle 50% at 24,529.97. General compute benchmarks record a PassMark CPU score of 20,317.86, alongside Geekbench results of 1,893.0 in single-core and 9,600.0 in multi-core metrics. In text-oriented and compression workloads, the server demonstrates strong results, achieving 2,604.0 in Geekbench text processing (top 25%) and 273.75 tokens per second in small model (135M) LLM text generation (top 25%). Memory throughput is standard, reaching 76.49 GB/sec read and 39.76 GB/sec write on 256 MB blocks.

The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU allocation delivers high dedicated CPU density without the added overhead of unneeded memory capacity. The instance lacks specialized instruction sets like AVX-512 and AMX, which limits its suitability for high-parameter machine learning training. However, the presence of dedicated AMD EPYC cores, AES and SHA-NI cryptographic hardware support, and fast local NVMe storage makes the c3-16-flex suitable for code compilation, CI/CD runners, batch compression, text processing, and compute-focused web services.
description: OVHcloud c3-16-flex is a compute-optimized instance built on the KVM hypervisor, featuring 8 dedicated x86_64 physical cores (8 vCPUs) from the AMD EPYC processor family operating at 2.3 GHz without hyperthreading. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM (2.0 GB per core), 50 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The system includes hardware support for AES, SHA-NI, and standard AVX extensions, though it lacks AVX-512 and AMX instructions. Benchmark testing indicates competitive compute capability, highlighted by strong top-quartile performance in stress-ng single-core tests, Geekbench text processing, and small-model LLM text generation. Other benchmarks, including a PassMark CPU score of 20,317.86 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 9,600.0, place it consistently in the mid-range tier. OVHcloud c3-16-flex is suited for compute-focused tasks requiring dedicated core execution, such as CI/CD pipelines, code compilation, static web serving, and lightweight batch processing.
